corpus.layout_note: Stored flat as <task>.json. The audit script censuses the live tree layout `<root>/*/verdicts/*.json`, so re-measuring the frozen copies means reshaping them first. The exact command is in `derivation_rule_mirrored.reproduce_frozen_census` — the script was deliberately NOT taught a second layout for a one-off measurement.

census_frozen.note_on_the_three_on_contract_issues: 54 issues - 51 off-contract = 3, and all three are task 2896's post-overwrite `suggestion` issues. In this corpus off_contract_severity and location_less are the SAME 51 records.

population_identity_check.question: Does the frozen corpus still contain exactly the findings the roster names?
population_identity_check.reading: The 22 live findings, the 22 frozen findings and 22 of the 23 roster entries are the SAME set. The one roster entry with no record anywhere is 2896's, which is the finding the overwrite destroyed. This is the completeness proof for the roster: it was transcribed from the task description, and it reconciles with the corpus exactly.

census_drift.why_this_is_a_finding_not_a_footnote: The task description's provenance stanza states six falsifiable measurements and concludes 'so this residue is closed-ended and will not grow'. It does not grow. It SHRINKS. Two of the six no longer hold, and both moved DOWNWARD because re-reviews overwrite verdict files in place. A triage whose job is honest accounting cannot restate a stale census as current fact, and this drift bounds how much of the residue is recoverable at all.

the_two_lost_findings_reconcile_exactly.reading: Exactly one finding was lost from each band. The one lost from the triage band is task 2896's `high` — the highest-severity finding in this task's own roster, and the only one already known to have been a genuine defect. The description called the population closed-ended; it lost its most important member in the three days between being written and being read.
the_two_lost_findings_reconcile_exactly.description_counted_four_highs: The description says 'the four `high` plus the one `major`'. Only 3 highs remain measurable. The missing fourth is 2896's. That single digit is the cleanest available proof of the erosion.

caveat_on_the_role_claim.measured: Two role spellings exist as verdict files in the tree: reviewer_comprehensive.json (1238 files) and merger.json (29 files). All 29 merger verdicts carry ZERO issues.
caveat_on_the_role_claim.why_it_matters: 'Every off-contract issue came from reviewer_comprehensive' is TRUE but nearly vacuous: reviewer_comprehensive is the only role that emits issues at all here, so the measurement does not single it out against peers. It is evidence about which role writes issues, not about which role writes them badly. Recorded because the description's phrasing invites the stronger reading.

the_two_gates_are_separate_populations.reading: The location-less defect is BROADER than the severity defect: 47 further findings lacked `location` while carrying a contract severity, including 2 `blocking` ones. Those 47 were still adjudicated, because severity is what the gates key on for scope. Only the 74 in the intersection were silently dropped. This is why the census keeps the two tallies separate — folding them together would hide that the two failures have different blast radii.

derivation_rule_mirrored.location_less_rule: issue has no non-blank `location` key, regardless of `file`/`line`
derivation_rule_mirrored.selection_rule: off_contract_severity AND triage_band; role is never a filter
derivation_rule_mirrored.id_rule: <task>-<category>-<index in verdict.issues[]>, so every id re-resolves against a frozen file
derivation_rule_mirrored.six_issue_schemas_normalized: headline from `title` else `short_summary`; primary detail from `description` else `detail` else `summary`; then `failure_scenario`/`reproduce`/`suggestion`/`suggested_fix`/`recommendation` appended when present. See scripts/audit_offcontract_review_findings.py::normalize_issue — the SPOT for the variance.
derivation_rule_mirrored.reproduce_frozen_census: F=$(mktemp -d)/task-meta; for f in docs/offcontract-review-finding-triage-2026-09-14/corpus/*.json; do t=$(basename "$f" .json); mkdir -p "$F/$t/verdicts"; cp "$f" "$F/$t/verdicts/reviewer_comprehensive.json"; done; python scripts/audit_offcontract_review_findings.py --root "$F" --json
